glossary.definition: The robust basic-attention phenomenon whereby observers reflexively shift attention toward the direction a depicted face is looking; imported into ad research to test whether a model's gaze steers attention toward the advertised product [FACT - Frontiers in Psychology 2017, PMC5454066 abstract; body 403-blocked so exact effect sizes are UNKNOWN].

A concept named in the specialist brief ('the attractiveness halo') that is NOT covered anywhere in this KB's grounding research file. Per the no-fabrication discipline it is held as an open UNKNOWN rather than backfilled from general training-data knowledge of the classic halo-effect literature; see ATTRACTIVENESS_HALO_RESEARCH_GAP.

A female body-shape ratio Singh (1993) proposed as a parsimonious attractiveness cue at ~0.7 combined with moderate weight; the clean 'universal 0.7' story is contested by Tassinary & Hansen's 1998 confound critique, Henss's differing 1995 replication, and cross-cultural samples (e.g. a Ugandan sample preferring ~0.5 and heavier weight) [FACT, contested — Sources 7-9].

The male-body dimorphism cue cross-culturally paired with female WHR in attractiveness research; upper-body-strength cues account for most of the variance in men's rated bodily attractiveness (PMC5745404), read as the V-taper being the supported target rather than maximal muscle mass [FACT - Sources 11, 12].

Frederick & Haselton's 2007 finding (PSPB, six studies) that moderate — not maximal — muscularity is rated most attractive; more-muscular men were rated sexier and more dominant but less committed as long-term mates, with a methodological caveat that the stimuli were drawings/CGI figures possibly biasing the 'moderate' optimum [FACT with caveat - Source 10].

Dunn & Searle's 2010 finding that identical models rated for attractiveness differ by sex when placed in a high-status car: the male target's rating rose significantly for female raters, while the female target's rating showed no such shift for male raters; one experimental paradigm, treated as a working hypothesis [FACT - Sources 13-15].

Horton & Wohl's (1956) framing of the one-sided emotional bond an audience forms with a media persona; a primary but not the most robust explanatory framework in influencer research, per Han et al. 2024's meta-analysis which ranks Source Credibility Theory highest [FACT - Source 18].

The Sirgy-lineage theory that persuasion rises when a brand/persona's symbolic image matches the consumer's self-concept; self-influencer congruence affects purchase intention indirectly, mediated by parasocial interaction and perceived altruistic motive [FACT - Sources 18, 19].

The saliency-map framework predicting fixations from low-level physical features (luminance/color contrast, orientation, motion/flicker) independent of semantic content; Cerf, Frady & Koch's face-detection channel is added on top of exactly this substrate [FACT - Source 1].

The house rule that attractiveness is delivered via styling, silhouette, status context, expression, and cinematography, never nudity/sexualized posing/solicitation; sourced from Meta's Adult Nudity and Sexual Activity community standard, which returned HTTP 403 through the proxy this session so the claim rests on an indexed summary, not a direct fetch, and must be re-verified live before shipping borderline content [FACT-from-indexed-summary, downgraded - Source 20].

nodes.definition: Establish the best-replicated finding in this KB: faces attract gaze early and largely independent of the viewing task. Cerf, Frady & Koch (Journal of Vision, 2009) tracked eye movements in free-viewing and search tasks and found adults preferentially fixate faces; adding a face-detection channel (Viola-Jones) to a bottom-up Itti-Koch saliency model raised fixation-prediction AUC from about 0.53 (classic bottom-up model alone) to over 0.84 [FACT - PubMed 20053101]. The pattern replicates in newer real-world-stimulus work (ACM ETRA 2020, 'Faces strongly attract early fixations in naturally sampled real-world stimulus materials') [FACT - Source 2]. The literature's interpretation is that face-fixation is a semantic/social pull, not explained by low-level physical saliency alone. Craft translation [ESTIMATE, high confidence]: in a 3-6 second reel frame, a human face is the near-certain first-fixation anchor, so composition should place the face where attention should START and use motion/composition to hand attention off from there.

included: the Cerf/Frady/Koch fixation-prediction AUC finding and its ETRA 2020 replication
the semantic/social-pull interpretation vs low-level saliency alone
the craft rule that a face is the near-certain first-fixation anchor
excluded: gaze-direction/cueing effects once a face is present (its own node)
motion/contrast as a separate bottom-up channel (its own node)

pros.claim: The face-fixation finding is one of the best-replicated results in this literature, giving a high-confidence composition anchor
pros.example: placing the persona's face at the frame's natural first-fixation point (e.g. upper third, well-lit) before any other element competes for attention

cons.claim: Over-relying on face-as-anchor without a deliberate hand-off can leave the product/setting under-attended for the whole clip
cons.example: a face-locked frame where the viewer's gaze never migrates to the product because no compositional or motion cue invites the hand-off

failure_modes: treating face-fixation as guaranteeing the VIEWER's subsequent attention path rather than just the first fixation
placing the face off-frame or poorly lit and expecting a bottom-up saliency element to substitute for it
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites the Cerf et al. AUC figures (~0.53 vs >0.84) and the ETRA 2020 replication, and states the craft rule that the face anchors first fixation with a deliberate hand-off to the rest of the frame
revisit_triggers: a newer eye-tracking study revises the AUC figures or contradicts the face-fixation-independent-of-task finding
a reel format (e.g. no visible face, voiceover-only) is tested and the anchor rule needs qualification

base.update_signal: a new eye-tracking study revises the fixation-prediction figures or the task-independence finding

nodes.definition: Name the central contested finding in the gaze literature: whether directing a model's gaze AT the product beats gaze AT the viewer is NOT settled. Sajjacholapunt & Ball (Frontiers in Psychology, 2014, PMC3941030) found AVERTED gaze (model looking toward the ad content, away from the viewer) improved attention/memory outcomes [FACT - Source 4]. Against this, a ResearchGate-hosted eye-tracking study reports face presence plus gaze directed TOWARD the product strongly influenced attention, memorization, ad/brand evaluation, and purchase intention [FACT - Source 5]. These two findings pull in different directions on what 'averted' vs 'toward-product' actually means for outcomes, and the broader literature does not uniformly show gaze-to-product beats gaze-to-viewer for downstream persuasion; direct gaze at the viewer independently drives engagement/arousal and trust signaling. Honest synthesis [ESTIMATE, medium confidence]: gaze cueing reliably moves ATTENTION; which direction wins on MEMORY/PURCHASE depends on goal and context and the sources disagree. Do not hard-code 'always look at the product' as a rule.

included: the Source 4 vs Source 5 conflict on gaze-to-product vs averted/gaze-to-viewer outcomes
the per-shot-A/B-variable rule this conflict forces
that attention-capture and persuasion-outcome are separate claims
excluded: the basic gaze-cueing phenomenon itself (its own node)
celebrity-status interaction with gaze (its own node)

pros.example: keeping gaze direction as a tagged A/B variable in shot planning instead of mandating 'model always looks at the product'

cons.claim: Refusing to pick a default gaze direction leaves craft decisions under-specified without a per-project test budget
cons.example: a small production with no A/B capacity having no default rule to fall back on for a single hero shot

nodes.definition: Establish the bottom-up saliency channel that operates alongside faces. The Itti-Koch lineage predicts fixations from low-level physical features: luminance/color contrast, orientation, and motion/flicker are strong exogenous-attention channels [FACT], and it is exactly this substrate Cerf et al. built their face-detection channel on top of. Motion is one of the most potent exogenous attention captures in that framework. Craft translation [ESTIMATE, high confidence]: a single moving element against a still field (a car door opening, hair moving, fabric catching wind) is a reliable attention magnet; competing motion everywhere destroys the cue. High local contrast on the intended focal point does the equivalent job for a still frame.

included: Itti-Koch bottom-up saliency channels (contrast, orientation, motion/flicker)
the single-moving-element-against-a-still-field craft rule
high local contrast as the still-frame equivalent
excluded: face-fixation itself (its own node)
the combined single-focal-subject composition rule (its own node)

pros.claim: A single, well-isolated motion or contrast cue reliably directs attention without needing a face in frame
pros.example: using one piece of fabric catching wind as the sole moving element in an otherwise still product shot

cons.claim: Multiple simultaneous motion sources compete and can null out any single intended cue, per the same saliency-map logic
cons.example: a shot with moving hair, moving fabric, and camera motion all at once, leaving no clear attention winner

failure_modes: stacking multiple uncoordinated motion cues in one frame
relying on motion alone in a still-image format where it cannot apply
acceptance_tests: the analysis names the Itti-Koch bottom-up channels (contrast, orientation, motion/flicker) as the substrate Cerf et al. extended, and states the single-moving-element / high-local-contrast craft rule
revisit_triggers: a frame is found with multiple competing motion sources and no clear attention winner

nodes.definition: Compose the cross-cutting rule that follows from combining face-first fixation with motion/contrast salience: one clear face, plus one motion cue, plus at most one status/luxury signal per short frame [ESTIMATE, high confidence, derived from A1.1 and A1.3]. Overloading a frame with multiple competing faces, multiple moving elements, or multiple status props kills the saliency advantage each individual cue would otherwise deliver, because the same bottom-up saliency competition that makes ONE motion cue effective also means MULTIPLE cues split attention and reduce the predictive strength of any single one.

pros.example: a shot brief that explicitly rejects a second background face or a second moving prop competing with the hero cue

cons.claim: A strict one-of-each cap can feel formulaic across a whole campaign if applied without variation in framing or pacing
cons.example: every shot in a series following the identical one-face/one-motion/one-status template and reading as visually repetitive

adding a second status prop (e.g. both a luxury car AND a luxury watch emphasized equally) and diluting the signal
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the one-face + one-motion-cue + one-status-signal-per-frame rule and explains it as following from bottom-up saliency competition destroying multiple simultaneous cues

nodes.definition: State the base finding on female body-shape attractiveness. Singh (1993) reported a lower waist-to-hip ratio (approximately 0.7) combined with moderate body weight was rated more attractive for female figures across observers, and proposed WHR as a parsimonious attractiveness cue [FACT - Sources 7, 8]. This is the foundational result the rest of the WHR literature qualifies, critiques, and complicates (its own node covers that contestation); taken alone, Singh's finding is a real, oft-cited result, not an invented one.

included: Singh 1993's WHR ~0.7 + moderate-weight finding as the base result
excluded: the methodological critique, cross-cultural contestation, and the non-universality conclusion (its own node)

pros.claim: Singh's WHR finding gives a simple, widely-cited quantitative anchor for silhouette-flattering styling
pros.example: tailoring that visually reads a lower WHR silhouette without any exposure, as a styling target grounded in a named study

cons.claim: Treating Singh's number alone, without its critiques, risks presenting a single 1993 study as a settled universal constant
cons.example: quoting '0.7 is the ideal WHR' as if no methodological or cross-cultural complication existed

failure_modes: citing the 0.7 figure without the accompanying contestation node
treating body weight as irrelevant when Singh's finding paired WHR with moderate weight
acceptance_tests: the analysis states Singh 1993's finding: lower WHR (~0.7) + moderate weight rated more attractive across observers, citing it as one foundational study
revisit_triggers: a new large-sample WHR study is published that either strengthens or further undermines the 0.7 anchor

base.update_signal: a new large-sample WHR study strengthens or undermines the 0.7 anchor

nodes.definition: Qualify the WHR finding with its methodological and cross-cultural record, because presenting 0.7 as a universal constant is the exact honesty failure this KB must avoid. Tassinary & Hansen (1998) criticized Singh's line-drawing stimuli for confounding WHR with waist size and body weight, and built 27 'unconfounded' stimuli that produced results complicating the clean 0.7 story; Henss (1995) replicated with somewhat different results; and cross-cultural work is mixed, with one study finding Ugandan raters preferred approximately 0.5 WHR and heavier weight [FACT, contested - Sources 8, 9]. Honest synthesis [ESTIMATE, medium confidence]: 'a broad tendency toward lower WHR in many populations' is defensible; '0.7 is a universal constant' is NOT — weight, culture, and stimulus artifacts all move it.

included: the Tassinary & Hansen confound critique
the Henss replication divergence
the Ugandan cross-cultural counter-finding
the 'broad tendency defensible, universal constant not' conclusion
excluded: Singh's base finding itself (its own node)
the male-side shoulder-to-hip pairing (its own node)

pros.claim: Carrying the critique and cross-cultural record prevents a studio style-guide from mis-citing a contested number as a hard universal target
pros.example: styling guidance that reads 'lower-WHR-flattering silhouette, broadly defensible' rather than 'hit exactly 0.7'

cons.claim: A qualified, non-universal conclusion gives less crisp guidance than a single hard number would for fast production decisions
cons.example: a stylist wanting one target ratio instead of a range qualified by culture and weight interaction

failure_modes: dropping the critique and citing 0.7 as a universal constant
over-correcting and dismissing WHR as having no attractiveness signal at all, which the broad-tendency finding does not support
acceptance_tests: the analysis cites the Tassinary & Hansen confound critique, the Henss replication, and the Ugandan cross-cultural counter-finding, and states the broad-tendency-defensible / universal-constant-not conclusion
revisit_triggers: a large modern cross-cultural WHR meta-analysis resolves the contested magnitude
a specific target market's own preference data becomes available and should override the general literature

base.update_signal: a large cross-cultural WHR meta-analysis or new market-specific preference data surfaces

nodes.definition: State the shape-of-the-curve finding for male attractiveness. Frederick & Haselton, 'Why Is Muscularity Sexy? Tests of the Fitness Indicator Hypothesis' (Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 2007), across six studies found MODERATE muscularity rated most attractive — an inverted-U, not 'more is better' — and that women rated more-muscular men as sexier and more physically dominant but LESS committed as long-term mates [FACT - Source 10]. A methodological caveat carried by the authors' critics: the studies used drawings/computer-generated male figures, some at supra-normal strength, which may bias where the 'moderate' optimum lands [FACT, caveat - Source 10 commentary]. The 'fitness indicator hypothesis' label is the ORIGINAL AUTHORS' evolutionary framing, reported here as their framing, not as this KB's established causal explanation.

included: the inverted-U shape (moderate beats maximal)
the sexier-but-less-committed rating split
the drawings/CGI stimulus caveat
labeling 'fitness indicator hypothesis' as the authors' own framing
excluded: the upper-body-strength-variance and V-taper finding (its own node)

nodes.definition: State the key asymmetric-by-sex status finding. Dunn & Searle, 'Effect of manipulated prestige-car ownership on both sex attractiveness ratings' (British Journal of Psychology, 2010, 101:69-80) placed the SAME models with the same expression/posture in a high-status car (silver Bentley Continental GT) versus a neutral car (red Ford Fiesta ST). A replication/extension, 'Luxurious cars increase perceptions of status, social dominance, and attractiveness' (Personality and Individual Differences, 2023), supports the status-to-attractiveness link [FACT - Source 15]. Read [ESTIMATE, medium-high confidence]: luxury-status props (car, watch, setting) plausibly lift the MALE persona's attractiveness signal to a female audience more than equivalent props lift the FEMALE persona's signal to a male audience — the leverage point of a 'classic-luxurious' genre — but this rests on one experimental paradigm plus one replication, not an established law.

nodes.definition: Establish parasocial relationship theory as one of the primary explanatory frameworks for influencer-style persona content. (2024), a meta-analysis of social-media-influencer impact (Psychology & Marketing, 250 effect sizes / 53 studies), finds Source Credibility Theory (trustworthiness, expertise) is the MOST robust explanatory framework, with Parasocial Interaction Theory and Congruity Theory also significant but secondary contributors to attitudinal outcomes [FACT - Source 18]. edges.resolution_rule: cap muscularity at the moderate, evident-not-extreme end of the inverted-U even when emphasizing the V-taper/strength cue; strength legibility, not maximal mass, is the target

edges.why_related: leaning into the WHR attraction cue for craft purposes is in tension with the documented body-dissatisfaction harm of idealized-body imagery the meta-analysis flags
edges.resolution_rule: the taste floor and ethics-link nodes govern: use silhouette/tailoring cues without amplifying toward the ultra-thin or ultra-idealized end the meta-analysis associates with harm

edges.why_related: the taste-floor claims rest on proxy-blocked, indexed-summary-only sourcing per the evidence hierarchy, yet the floor is still treated as a hard, non-negotiable constraint
edges.resolution_rule: treat the floor as binding despite the fetch gap (fail closed on a compliance question), and require a live re-fetch of the policy text before shipping any borderline styling

edges.why_related: treating parasocial bonding and status-aspiration as freely interchangeable levers is in tension with Han et al.'s finding that source credibility, not parasocial bonding, is the most robust framework
edges.resolution_rule: do not treat parasocial bonding as the primary mechanism; foreground credibility/trust signaling and use parasocial bonding and aspiration as secondary, content-type-specific levers

edges.why_related: the instinct to fill the named halo-effect gap with well-known 'what is beautiful is good' literature from memory is in direct tension with the no-fabrication discipline
edges.resolution_rule: the no-laundering/no-fabrication rule wins: leave the halo effect as a named research gap and do not backfill it from training-data memory, however well-established the effect is believed to be

edges.why_related: the original authors' 'fitness indicator hypothesis' evolutionary framing is in tension with reporting only the measured inverted-U rating pattern without adopting their causal story
edges.resolution_rule: report the measured pattern (moderate muscularity rated most attractive) and label the fitness-indicator hypothesis as the authors' own framing, without asserting it as this KB's established causal explanation

edges.why_related: a craft table wants a crisp default gaze-direction rule per persona, which is in tension with the underlying literature's unresolved gaze-to-product-vs-viewer disagreement
edges.resolution_rule: keep gaze direction flagged as a per-shot A/B variable inside the craft table rather than hard-coding a single default, even though this makes the table less crisp

edges.why_related: both are dimorphism-paired body-shape attraction cues from the same cross-cultural pairing literature — WHR for women, shoulder-to-hip V-taper for men — the two halves of one paired-cue paradigm
the documented psychological harm from idealized imagery causally motivates holding the aspirational-not-explicit taste floor as an ethical, not merely legal, constraint
the status-x-gaze interaction found for higher-status personas causally informs how gaze should be handled in the status-cue-heavy male-persona craft cell
when craft-table choices are field-tested (A/B'd) in production, the results should feed back into how strongly each underlying contested finding is weighted
the platform taste floor constrains which craft-table translations are permissible regardless of what the attention/attraction research alone would suggest
the ethics link constrains the craft table to hold the aspirational-not-degrading line independent of platform enforcement strength
in composing a frame, the face-first fixation anchor is established before the motion/contrast cue that hands attention off from it

conflict_axes.name: face_first_fixation_vs_competing_motion
conflict_axes.description: Placing the face as the primary attention anchor is in tension with adding motion cues that, if uncoordinated, compete with and dilute that same anchor.
poles: face as the sole primary anchor
motion cue competing for the same attention budget
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use exactly one coordinated motion cue that hands attention off FROM the face rather than competing with it

conflict_axes.name: gaze_to_product_vs_gaze_to_viewer
conflict_axes.description: The literature disagrees on whether directing an ad model's gaze at the product (Source 5) or an averted/viewer-directed gaze (Source 4) produces better memory/purchase outcomes.
poles: gaze directed at the product
gaze directed at or averted from the viewer
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat gaze direction as a per-shot A/B variable rather than a hard-coded default

conflict_axes.name: whr_universal_constant_vs_culture_and_weight_confound
conflict_axes.description: Singh's ~0.7 WHR finding is challenged by Tassinary & Hansen's confound critique, Henss's differing replication, and cross-cultural counter-findings, so a universal-constant reading is not supportable.
poles: 0.7 WHR as a universal attractiveness constant
culture- and weight-dependent, confound-qualified tendency
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use 'broad tendency toward lower WHR' as the defensible claim and drop any universal-constant framing

conflict_axes.name: muscularity_more_is_better_vs_inverted_u_optimum
conflict_axes.description: A naive 'more muscularity is more attractive' reading is directly contradicted by Frederick & Haselton's inverted-U finding that moderate muscularity is rated most attractive.
poles: maximal muscularity reads as most attractive
moderate, inverted-U optimum is most attractive
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: target the moderate/evident-not-extreme optimum and treat the upper-body-strength-variance finding as sharpening, not overriding, the inverted-U shape

conflict_axes.name: status_prop_lift_symmetric_vs_asymmetric_by_sex
conflict_axes.description: Dunn & Searle found a status prop (the car) boosted the male target's rated attractiveness for female raters but not the female target's rating for male raters — an asymmetric, not symmetric, effect.
poles: status props lift attractiveness equally for both personas
status props lift the male persona's rating asymmetrically more
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: weight status-prop investment toward the male-persona aspiration lever per the asymmetric finding, while treating it as one paradigm not settled law

conflict_axes.name: idealized_imagery_attention_value_vs_documented_harm
conflict_axes.description: Idealized body imagery reliably captures attention and drives aspiration, while Grabe, Ward & Hyde's meta-analysis documents measurable body-dissatisfaction harm from exactly that kind of imagery.
poles: maximize idealized-imagery attention/aspiration value
avoid the documented body-image harm of idealized imagery
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the aspirational-not-degrading taste floor as the resolution: use styling/status/silhouette cues without amplifying toward the ultra-idealized end flagged as harmful

conflict_axes.name: aspiration_lever_vs_identification_lever
conflict_axes.description: Aspiration (wanting to become/possess what the persona has, the status route) and identification (self-congruity/trust, the parasocial route) are two distinct mechanisms that can be conflated if a single content strategy tries to pull both without distinguishing them.
poles: aspiration/status-driven persuasion
identification/self-congruity-driven persuasion
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: diagnose each content piece's intended lever explicitly (luxury-place/car content = aspiration; quote/travel-relatable content = identification) rather than blending both by default

conflict_axes.name: source_credibility_vs_parasocial_as_dominant_mechanism
conflict_axes.description: Han et al.'s meta-analysis ranks Source Credibility Theory as the most robust explanatory framework for influencer impact, which is in tension with treating parasocial bonding as the headline mechanism this KB's aspiration/identification framing might suggest.
poles: parasocial bonding as the primary driver
source credibility as the most robust, primary driver
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: foreground credibility/trustworthiness/expertise signaling in persona scripting and treat parasocial bonding and self-congruity as significant secondary contributors, per the meta-analytic ranking

conflict_axes.name: indexed_summary_evidence_vs_directly_fetched_fact
conflict_axes.description: Several claims (the taste floor, the gaze-cueing ad study) rest on proxy-blocked pages and indexed summaries rather than a direct fetch, creating tension between treating them as usable now versus withholding them until verified.
poles: use the indexed-summary claim now, appropriately downgraded
withhold the claim entirely until a direct fetch is possible
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the downgraded claim now but carry the block inline and require re-verification before any high-stakes (e.g. compliance-adjacent) decision relies on it exclusively

conflict_axes.name: evo_psych_causal_framing_vs_agnostic_effect_reporting
conflict_axes.description: Original authors' evolutionary fitness-indicator framing for the muscularity finding is in tension with reporting only the measured rating-pattern effect without adopting their causal explanation as this KB's own.
poles: adopt the authors' evolutionary fitness-indicator explanation as the causal story
report only the measured effect, labeling the evolutionary framing as the authors', not this KB's, claim
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always report the measured pattern first and attribute any evolutionary causal framing explicitly to its original authors, never as this KB's independent conclusion

priority_rationale: The attention-foundations nodes (face-fixation, gaze cueing and its contested direction, motion/contrast salience, the single-focal-subject rule) come first because every downstream composition and craft choice is read against them; the attraction-cue nodes (WHR and its contestation, muscularity's inverted-U and upper-body-strength/V-taper, the status-cue asymmetry, the idealized-imagery harm evidence) come next as the body of body-shape and status research each craft cell must trace to; the aspiration/identification nodes (parasocial theory, self-congruity, the two-lever synthesis) follow as the persuasion-mechanism layer; the craft nodes (the gendered translation table, the taste floor, the ethics-taste link) compose all of the above into shippable, floor-compliant guidance; and the evidence-discipline nodes (the tiering hierarchy, the no-laundering rule, the named halo-effect gap) come last because they are the meta-level discipline that keeps every node above honest about what is FACT, what is DOWNGRADED, what is ESTIMATE, and what is simply not yet known.
